The volume of total crude oil and petroleum product imports rose in February to 320.9 million barrels from 303.2 million in January. The total value fell to $6.64 billion in February from $6.83 billion. These data are available only on a Census basis.

The price of imported crude oil fell to an average $20.21 a barrel in February from $21.99 per barrel in January. This was the first drop in eight months. The value of February crude oil imports rose to $5.28 billion from $5.11 billion.

The United States registered a trade surplus of $291 million with Western Europe and $944 million with the United Kingdom in February. Both figures were the best U.S. trade performance since March 1994, and primarily reflected a big surge in aircraft exports to the United Kingdom.

The balance-of-payments basis for recording U.S. trade via receipts from and payments to other countries includes adjustments for military shipments, nonmonetary gold, and inland freight trade with Canada and Mexico.
Census basis data uses information collected by the U.S. Customs Service on goods shipped across U.S. borders.
